Steel production is, at its core, a resource-intensive undertaking that draws heavily upon the natural environment, including land, water, and raw materials. As a result, our operations inevitably interact with the ecosystems and species that inhabit the landscapes in which we operate. This interdependence cuts both ways. On one hand, we possess significant natural capital dependencies by dint of which our operational resilience remains inextricably tethered to the health, stability, and integrity of surrounding ecosystems. On the other hand, the pressures associated with industrial activity can adversely affect these very ecosystems if not managed with rigour and care. Our commitment to biodiversity management stems from this dual commitment—of dependency and responsibility in equal measure—and induces us to move decisively beyond a compliance-oriented posture toward one grounded in genuine ecological accountability and a determination to leave the natural environments in which we operate measurably better than we found them. 

### **No net loss of Biodiversity** 

approach aligned with internationally recognised standards and frameworks, including the TNFD LEAP approach, IFC Performance Standard 6, IUCN guidance, the Biodiversity Protocol, and relevant national regulatory requirements. Building on this foundation, the approach also incorporates the Double-Entry Bookkeeping (DEBK) methodology under the Biodiversity Protocol and the IUCN Biodiversity Indicator and Reporting System (BIRS), enabling us to account for historical ecosystem losses and gains in a structured and comparable manner. 

We have set ourselves the clear mandate of achieving NNL of biodiversity across our operational footprint by 2030. In pursuit of this objective, we have adopted a structured mitigation hierarchy—Avoid, Minimise, Restore, and Offset—which now serves as the foundational framework guiding how we assess, manage, and mitigate biodiversity impacts across the lifecycle of our operations and projects. Critically, we have not confined this framework to our environmental function; rather, we have embedded it within our Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework, positioning nature-related considerations alongside financial, operational, climate, and reputational risks and opportunities in decision-making processes across all levels of the organisation. 

Within this overarching methodology, we track biodiversity impact across four interrelated dimensions: the extent of land disturbed, restored, and actively managed; the ecological functionality and resilience of restored habitats; the status of species of conservation significance; and the condition of critical ecosystem services, including water regulation and soil conservation. Together, these dimensions provide the analytical breadth and methodological rigour required to consistently assess, quantify, and benchmark biodiversity impacts across our diverse operational contexts. 

### **Measurement Framework and Disclosures** 

Credible progress towards NNL demands rigorous, scientifically grounded measurement of biodiversity impacts. Thus, we have developed a site-level biodiversity assessment and accounting 

In FY 2025–26, we completed baseline biodiversity assessments at our Dolvi, Salem, and Vasind facilities, establishing a robust foundation for ongoing impact measurement, performance tracking, and long-term target setting across these sites. We also took a further step toward greater transparency and accountability in managing our nature-related impacts and dependencies by publishing our first TNFD-aligned report: a comprehensive disclosure canvassing our governance approach, strategic priorities, naturerelated risks and opportunities, natural capital dependencies, and biodiversity performance. In doing so, we reaffirmed our belief that meaningful progress on biodiversity must be visible, verifiable, and open to scrutiny from all stakeholders with an interest in how we manage our relationship with the natural world. 



**Our first TNFD-Aligned Report:** A comprehensive disclosure encapsulating our governance approach, strategic priorities, and nature-related impacts, dependencies, risks, and opportunities.

## **Forging symbiotic human-nature relationships** 

Human-animal conflict remains one of the primary drivers of the unfettered loss of biodiversity unfolding across the planet. This problem is particularly acute in hilly regions, where dense forests teeming with a vast array of animal species co-exist alongside large-scale mining developments employing hundreds of human workers. 

Barbil, one such region home to our mining operations, has witnessed a rising frequency of human-elephant conflicts in recent years. Elephants from nearby forests have trespassed into farms and villages, fomenting panic among nearby settlements and resulting in widespread damage to both crops and property; unfortunately, in some cases, residents have responded to these encounters aggressively, leading to elephant deaths. 

At JSW Steel, we recognise that elephants constitute keystone species that play a pivotal role in maintaining the resilience of the ecosystems they inhabit. Therefore, we set ourselves the goal to address their loss by fostering a more symbiotic relationship between elephants and local communities in the areas surrounding our operations in Barbil. 

To this end, we entered into a partnership with the SAGE Foundation and the local Forest Department. Together, we focused on awareness raising, striving to help communities cultivate a better understanding of the importance of preserving elephants, and capacity building, helping communities implement non-kinetic measures, such as solar-powered streetlights, trip alarms, blinking lights, and fences, to prevent elephant encounters without inflicting any damage on the creatures. These measures have enabled 38 villages, with a combined population of nearly 20,000, to successfully manage 45 elephant encounters, demonstrating our commitment to fostering harmonious coexistence between people and nature.

The safe management of tailings remains among our highest environmental priorities, given its direct implications for the health of nearby communities and the integrity of surrounding ecosystems. Our approach to tailings management extends well beyond safe containment: we treat tailings as a resource rather than a liability. Across our mines, we have installed state-of-the-art containment systems and established tailings ponds to store intercepted materials securely. Where feasible, we recover valuable minerals from stored tailings; where recovery is not viable, we ensure safe storage. This approach minimises waste, reduces the environmental footprint of our operations, and generates cost savings by limiting the need for waste transport and external disposal.

## **Responsible tailings Tailings governance management framework** 

The responsible management of tailings is fundamental to our commitment to environmental stewardship, operational excellence and sustainable mining. We recognise that effective tailings management is critical to protecting our employees, host communities, the environment and the long-term value of our operations. Our approach is based on sound engineering principles, robust governance, proactive risk management and continuous monitoring throughout the lifecycle of our Tailings Storage Facilities (TSFs). 

› Our Tailings Management Framework is designed to ensure that tailings storage facilities are managed in alignment with recognised international good practices, applicable regulatory requirements, and internal management standards. The framework establishes clear governance, accountability, and oversight to support the safe and responsible management of tailings-related risks. 

Together, these standards provide a (TSFs). structured approach to identifying, Our tailings ponds aim to blend assessing and managing tailings-related environmental safety with resource risks while ensuring compliance with recovery and circularity. legislative obligations and industry best practice. 

While they incorporate advanced lining systems and geotechnical measures to enhance safety, they also serve as closed-loop systems, wherein the water consumed in beneficiation is virtually completely reclaimed and recycled through thickening, paste backfill methods, and intricate piping systems. We further strive to regularly implement structural reinforcements to ensure seismic safety and curb seepage. 

The integrity and performance of our tailings storage facilities are continuously monitored through a comprehensive inspection and assurance programme. This programme is designed to identify potential risks early, verify compliance with operating requirements and support continual improvement. 

Key activities include: 

- › Routine operational inspections in accordance with established checklists. 

- › Surveys to monitor facility condition, embankment stability and storage capacity. 

## **A nature-positive approach to responsible mining** 

› Applicable audits conducted to promote consistency, knowledge sharing and adherence to company standards. 

While mining is widely perceived as a significant driver of biodiversity loss, we firmly believe that meaningful opportunities exist to reverse this trend. We therefore conduct detailed impact assessments to identify potential threats our mining activities pose to local biodiversity and implement targeted interventions in response. These include the establishment of wildlife corridors to allow local fauna to navigate areas surrounding our mines safely, the creation of buffer zones to safeguard keystone species and critical ecosystems, and sustained investment in habitat restoration. Awareness programmes, which equip our workforce with a thorough understanding of local biodiversity and the role they can play in its protection, complement these measures. 

Findings from inspections and audits are tracked through formal action management processes, with corrective actions monitored to completion and lessons incorporated into operational practices. 

## **Re-envisaging mine-to-plant logistics for environmental gains and operational efficiencies** 

When assessing the environmental impacts of mining, attention tends to concentrate on the extraction stage. Yet the transportation of mined materials carries equally consequential, and frequently underappreciated, environmental costs, including greenhouse gas emissions, air and noise pollution, and habitat fragmentation. 

To manage these overlook socio-environmental consequences, we have focused on engineering sustainable transportation systems that simultaneously reduce environmental impact and improve the speed and efficiency with which mined materials reach their point of use. Our 24-kilometre pipe conveyor system, which transports iron ore fines from our captive mines to our largest Integrated Steel Plant at Vijayanagar, stands as the most prominent expression of this commitment. By displacing truck-based transport at scale, the system has materially reduced greenhouse gas emissions, curbed dust and noise pollution, and shortened transport timelines— concurrently advancing the sustainability and operational efficiency of our mining operations.

## **Reducing fossil fuel dependency across mining sites** 



### 

Reducing fossil fuel dependency across dispersed mining operations presents a distinct set of challenges. Unlike centralised industrial facilities, mine sites are often geographically isolated from established grid infrastructure and must maintain a reliable energy supply across multiple locations simultaneously. Historically, diesel generators have served as the most practical solution, owing to their ease of deployment and ability to provide dependable, dispatchable power on demand. 

However, extensive reliance on diesel generation carries a significant GHG footprint and exposes operations to the cost volatility associated with fossil fuel procurement. Recognising these risks, our Vijayanagar mining operations took a deliberate step toward reducing diesel dependency in FY 2025-26 by expanding solar installations across all nine mines in the region. These installations generated 32,908 kWh of clean energy over the course of the year. 

# **32,908 kWh** 

Clean energy generated across mining operations in FY 2025-26 

Together, these measures contributed to a measurable reduction in GHG emissions and lowered our dependence on externally procured fossil fuels. More importantly, they reflect a broader conviction that guides our approach to sustainable mining: the transition to cleaner energy is not limited to our steelmaking processes but is equally achievable, and equally necessary, across every stage of the value chain, from the extraction of raw materials at mines to the delivery of finished steel to our customers.

The sustainability of our operations and the health, well-being, and welfare of the communities living near our facilities are not separate considerations; they remain inherently and inextricably linked. Steel production entails multiple industrial processes that, in the absence of appropriate safeguards, hold the potential to exacerbate air, noise, and water pollution, with direct and measurable consequences for surrounding communities. We recognise this intersection not as a risk we must manage at arm's length but as a responsibility that sits at the centre of how we design and implement our operational strategy. 



› **Engagement** reflects our commitment to active, ongoing dialogue with the communities we affect and incorporating their perspectives into our decision-making processes, promoting public participation in our initiatives, and integrating traditional ecological knowledge where available and relevant. 

### **Our community engagement framework** 

### **Local employment and community skills development approach** 

To translate this commitment into structured, accountable action, we have adopted a community engagement framework centred on four core steps: identification, prevention, engagement, and surveillance. 

We also remain steadfast in our commitment to creating opportunities for local communities and strengthening regional economies. We offer training programmes to enhance the employability of local individuals, equipping them with skills relevant to our operations, and recruit them on a case-by-case basis, depending on operational requirements. Given our extensive operations across different regions in India, we define ‘local’ at the country level (i.e., India). Thus, at the site level, all employees are recruited from within India, and all senior management roles are filled by individuals recruited from within the country. 

   - › **Surveillance** ensures that the 

- › **Identification** involves the systematic mapping of communities in our operations' vicinity, the potential environmental and social impacts our activities may generate, and the specific vulnerabilities and needs of affected populations. 

- › **Prevention** directs us to design our operations and sustainability interventions in ways that anticipate and avoid unintended consequences for local communities before they arise, rather than responding to them after they transpire. 

impacts of our operations and the outcomes of our interventions are monitored continuously, enabling us to identify emerging concerns early and adapt our approach accordingly. 

Together, these four principles form the foundation of a framework that seeks to not only protect communities from the potential adverse effects of our operations but also help them cultivate a deeper understanding of contemporary environmental challenges, their complex impacts, and the adaptation and mitigation strategies available to them.

## **Alleviating water stress through community engagement** 

### 

We regularly conduct needs assessments across communities located near our operations to identify the most pressing socio-economic challenges burdening local populations and to ensure the implementation of high-impact interventions with the greatest potential to uplift their quality of life. The findings stemming from a recent assessment conducted in Barbil indicated that limited access to safe and clean drinking water remained one of the foremost challenges hindering local communities’ ability to live a safe and healthy life. 

Accordingly, in coherence with our commitment to ensuring the well-being of local communities affected by our operations, we implemented two key measures to mitigate this concern. Firstly, to provide immediate relief in the short run, we deployed 12 drinking water tankers across various regions near our mining operations. We strategically deployed these tankers in areas with high population densities to ensure that the benefits they provide accrue to as large a swath of individuals as possible. Additionally, in the long term, we installed solar-powered bore wells equipped with overhead tanks connected to tap water systems in nearby villages, systematically targeting the communities most vulnerable to water scarcity first. 

Over the past three years, we have constructed 51 such bore wells across 47 habitations in 32 villages, benefiting nearly 13,427 people. The introduction of solar-powered bore wells has generated several benefits for residents, including bolstering their access to potable water and allaying the physical hardship (i.e., drudgery) faced predominantly by women in collecting water from open wells often located miles away from their homes. 

# **51** 

Solar-powered bore wells constructed 

Overall, by adopting this multifaceted approach to strengthening water security in a traditionally water-scarce region, we have reinforced our commitment to participatory, people-first solutions that directly counteract socio-economic issues impinging on the quality of life of communities and their most marginalised residents touched by our operations.

Climate change and the transition to net zero represent tectonic shifts for the steel sector. They are not only giving rise to various physical and transition risks and opportunities that, if not managed effectively, could jeopardise the continuity of the industry's operations but are also fundamentally altering prevailing demand patterns for steel products. In particular, the growing global emphasis on sustainability, coupled with an upswing in climate-conscious consumerism, is gradually increasing demand for cleaner, low-carbon materials and greater transparency regarding the sustainability performance of products. 

Maintaining competitiveness in an era where rapid decarbonisation promises to reshape every aspect of society, be it infrastructure, manufacturing, or transportation, requires businesses to innovate new products and concomitantly embed the principles of sustainability and responsible climate stewardship at the very core of their product innovation processes. With this in mind, we are endeavouring to re-envision our existing products and design new offerings that deliver superior performance, enhance the sustainability of our operations, and hold the potential to serve as catalysts for our growth in this era of mounting climate action. In concurrence, we are enhancing the availability and quality of sustainabilityrelated product information, enabling customers and other stakeholders to better understand the environmental attributes and lifecycle impacts of our offerings. 

### **Certified for product sustainability** 

eco-labels, which signal a product’s superior environmental performance to consumers and foster more informed, data-driven purchasing decisions. 

As the transition to a low-carbon economy gains irreversible momentum, we recognise that accurately and effectively communicating our products' environmental footprint to customers is becoming indispensable for sustaining business growth and expanding our customer base. Therefore, we have intensified our pursuit of globally recognised third-party sustainability certifications in recent years. 

### **GreenPro certification** 

The highly coveted GreenPro certification, conferred by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), is one such example. Companies receive GreenPro certification based on an intricate and stringent life cycle assessment process that systematically examines a product's environmental impact at every stage of its lifecycle, spanning raw material extraction, manufacturing, usage, and end-of-life disposal. The receipt of this certification indicates a company's commitment to sustainable practices and provides consumers with confidence that the product satisfies industry-leading environmental standards. 

The application process for these certifications typically entails rigorous assessments that evaluate the environmental performance of a company’s products. By successfully completing these assessments and meeting a set of other prerequisites, firms earn the right to use accompanying 



Over the past few years, we have significantly broadened our portfolio of GreenPro-certified products. Most notably, we have established ourselves as one of India's first steelmakers to earn GreenPro certification for automotive-grade steel products. We believe these products will play a pivotal role in helping our customers in the auto-manufacturing sector reduce the environmental footprint of their products and, in turn, meet the mounting demand for more sustainably produced vehicles, with lower embedded emissions, spurred by evolving customer preferences and regulatory changes. 

### **Empowering Informed purchasing choices through EPDs** 

As demand for cleaner and greener products rises, sustainability is emerging not only as a potent value-creation lever but also as a vital product differentiation strategy. While customers are increasingly factoring environmental indicators, such as embedded emissions, water usage, and waste generation, into their purchasing decisions, this information is often unavailable or difficult to access, resulting in a gap between consumer intent and informed choice. 

At JSW Steel, we remain committed to bridging this lacuna by equipping our customers with accurate and up-todate information needed to evaluate the sustainability performance of our products holistically. We accordingly undertake meticulous LCAs across our key product lines, examining their environmental impacts, and publicly disclose the findings through detailed, third-party-verified EPDs. In doing so, we strengthen both the transparency and traceability of our products' environmental impacts for our customers. 

**Read more - EPDs** 

### **JSW GreenEdge: Our certificate-based solution for lower-carbon steel** 

JSW GreenEdge is our certificate-based solution designed to enable customers to access lower-carbon emissions steel while supporting the transition to a decarbonised steel value chain. This approach recognises the inherent complexity of decarbonising steel production and provides a credible, transparent mechanism to connect emissions reduction efforts at source with customer demand for sustainable materials. 

Under the GreenEdge framework, emissions reductions are generated through dedicated decarbonisation initiatives implemented across JSW Steel’s operations and value chain. These initiatives include improvements in energy efficiency, increased use of renewable energy, process optimisation, circularity measures, and deployment of breakthrough technologies. All reductions achieved are independently verified to ensure accuracy, credibility, and alignment with global best practices. 

These verified emissions reductions are converted into certificates, which are then allocated to customers based on predefined rules. The framework is operationalised in alignment with internationally recognised chain-of-custody principles, including ISO 22095, ensuring traceability, transparency, and auditability of claims. Robust governance mechanisms underpin the system, including clear boundaries, allocation methodologies, third-party assurance, and comprehensive documentation to prevent double counting and ensure credibility of claims. 

#### **Key features of JSW GreenEdge** 

**Read more - GreenEdge** 

JSW GreenEdge offers several key advantages to customers: 

1. Access to lower-carbon emissions steel. 

2. Credible and verifiable claims, supported by independent certification. 

3. Alignment with emerging market expectations, including evolving carbon disclosure and procurement requirements. 

4. Flexibility to integrate sustainability into procurement strategies. 

For JSW Steel, GreenEdge represents a strategic enabler to accelerate investments in decarbonisation while responding to growing market demand for low-carbon materials. It bridges the gap between current technological constraints and future pathways to near-zero steel, enabling immediate climate action. Through JSW GreenEdge, we are not only reducing emissions within our operations but also empowering our customers to participate meaningfully in the low-carbon transition—building a more sustainable and resilient steel ecosystem.

# JSW SPOTLIGHT 

JSW Spotlight is our Company’s flagship recognition and rewards platform, designed to bring employee achievements and appreciation to the forefront. It enables both peer-topeer and manager-led recognition, while also driving engagement through awareness sessions, contests and awards across business units. The platform plays a significant role in celebrating diverse talent, including dedicated initiatives that recognise and highlight the contributions of women employees. By fostering a consistent and visible culture of recognition, JSW Spotlight strengthens employee engagement and supports a more connected, motivated and high-performing workforce. 



## **JSW – She Leads Programme** 

The #SheLeads recognition campaign was launched on the JSW Spotlight platform to celebrate and acknowledge the contributions of women employees across JSW business units. Conducted in March 2026, the campaign enabled a defined group of managers to recognise women team members by sharing #SheLeads e-cards aligned with JSW’s five core values - Commitment, Courage, Agility, Collaboration and Compassion. 

At the conclusion of the campaign, recognitions were evaluated based on the number received and their alignment with organisational values. The top 100 women employees were identified and recognised for their contributions. Winners received merchandise, vouchers and recognition points credited to their Spotlight accounts. The initiative successfully highlighted inspiring contributions, fostered a culture of appreciation and showcased the impact of women employees across our Company.

## **Great People Manager (GPM)** 

## **Cheers** 

The Great People Manager (GPM) initiative is a nomination-based recognition programme designed to celebrate managers who demonstrate exceptional people leadership. Employees across our organisation were invited to nominate their managers, creating a strong bottom-up approach to recognition based on real experiences and impact. A total of 661 managers were nominated and recognised through this initiative. 

‘3 Cheers’ is a year-round peer-to-peer recognition programme designed to embed appreciation into our Company’s everyday culture. The initiative enables employees across all levels and functions to recognise one another in real time, making appreciation more frequent, inclusive and accessible. Through this programme, over 2,453 recognitions were shared, fostering a culture of appreciation and positive reinforcement across the organisation. 

The programme honoured leaders who consistently foster team development, mentorship, empathy, engagement and alignment with organisational values. Shortlisted managers were recognised through a structured rewards and recognition framework, reinforcing clear benchmarks for people leadership excellence at JSW. The initiative underscored the importance of leadership that places people at the centre and inspires teams to perform at their best. 

By encouraging employees to acknowledge both everyday contributions and significant achievements, the initiative strengthens cross-functional collaboration, builds stronger workplace relationships and promotes a positive feedback culture. Over time, ‘3 Cheers’ has successfully transformed recognition from a periodic activity into a continuous habit, contributing meaningfully to higher employee engagement and a more supportive work environment.

## **DEI sensitisation and allyship for inclusive leadership** 

### **DEI sensitisation workshops** 

These workshops are designed to create awareness around unconscious bias, privilege, microaggressions and inclusive language. Tailored sessions are conducted for employees, managers and leadership teams to strengthen understanding and encourage more inclusive workplace behaviours. 

### **Allyship in action** 

This initiative encourages active allyship across all levels of the organisation by empowering individuals to advocate for equity and inclusion. It promotes behaviours such as speaking up, creating safe spaces and amplifying underrepresented voices to foster a more inclusive workplace culture. 

### **Inclusive leadership programmes** 

These programmes equip leaders with the mindset and capabilities required to lead diverse teams effectively. Key focus areas include empathy-driven leadership, psychological safety and equitable decision-making, enabling leaders to build more collaborative and inclusive teams. 

### **Strengthening inclusion through capability building** 

At JSW, we remain committed to embedding Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) into our organisational culture. As part of this commitment, we have introduced a series of structured workshops aimed at deepening employees’ understanding of inclusive practices and equipping them with the tools required to foster a more open, respectful and equitable workplace. 

These workshops are designed to build awareness, encourage behavioural change and strengthen inclusive leadership across all levels of our Company. 

### **DEI sensitisation workshop (For all employees)** 

This workshop focuses on building foundational awareness and a shared understanding of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) across the organisation. Key focus areas include: 

- › Understanding the dimensions and definitions of DEI 

- › Exploring the business case for DEI within JSW 

- › Identifying challenges faced by diverse talent groups 

- › Recognising individual and systemic barriers to inclusion 

### **Allyship and inclusive leadership workshop** 

This advanced workshop is designed to enable leaders to actively foster inclusion within their teams. Key areas covered include: 

- › Understanding microaggressions and their impact in the workplace 

- › Building inclusive leadership behaviours and mindsets 

- › Practical tools to foster a culture of belonging 

- › Defining the role and different forms of active allyship 

The sessions are facilitated by experienced DEI practitioners and incorporate interactive discussions, real-world scenarios and actionable frameworks to ensure meaningful learning and practical application. 

Through these focused interventions, JSW continues to strengthen its inclusive culture by building awareness, enhancing leadership capability and empowering employees to contribute towards a more equitable, respectful and inclusive workplace. 



## **Women of future 2.0: Building a future-ready leadership pipeline** 

At JSW, we believe that a diverse and inclusive leadership pipeline is critical to driving sustainable growth and innovation. Women of Future 2.0, one of our flagship leadership development initiatives, reflects this commitment by empowering aspiring women leaders to grow with confidence, capability and influence. 

Designed as a structured seven-month journey, the programme focuses on strengthening leadership. It equips participants with the mindset and capabilities required to navigate complexity, lead with impact and step into future-ready roles. 

The programme brings together high-potential women employees who demonstrate strong performance, leadership potential and a growth mindset. Through a blend of immersive learning interventions, mentorship from senior leaders and action-learning projects, participants gain practical exposure to real business challenges while strengthening their strategic and leadership capabilities. 

Women of Future 2.0 is designed to: 

- › Build self-awareness, resilience and confidence 

- › Strengthen empathetic and accountable leadership 

- › Enhance strategic thinking and business decision-making 

- › Develop executive presence for larger leadership roles 

- › Enable experiential learning through action-driven projects 

Building on the strong foundation of the initiative, we have already engaged more than 200 women employees across JSW, reflecting both the scale and impact of the programme. 

## **A continuous journey** 

At JSW Steel, we believe that diversity is reflected through representation, while inclusion is experienced through a genuine sense of belonging. We remain committed to continuously strengthening our policies, practices and organisational culture to build a truly inclusive workplace, one that values diverse perspectives and leverages them to drive innovation, collaboration and long-term success.

# KEY STRATEGIES FOR HEALTH AND SAFETY 

In FY 2025–26, our health and safety agenda was driven by a structured, four-pillar framework anchored to Vision 2030: Zero Harm, comprising Effective Leadership, Robust Systems, Competent Workforce and Digitalisation & Innovation. Each pillar represents a mutually reinforcing dimension of safety excellence, collectively building towards a workplace where every individual returns home safe, every day.

### **Safety observations and frontline accountability** 

### **Lead the Change – Safety as a Core Value** 

Visible, accountable and committed leadership is the bedrock of any highperforming safety culture. At JSW Steel, safety leadership is not confined to the EHS function; it is a shared responsibility that extends across every level of management, from the Board and senior executives to line managers and frontline supervisors. Our Company’s approach rests on the principle that leaders who are actively present on the shop floor, who participate in safety observations, and who model safety-conscious behaviour, drive the strongest outcomes. In FY 2025-26, several structured initiatives reinforced this philosophy. 

Safety observations are among the most powerful leading indicators of cultural maturity. They signal an organisation’s ability to identify and address unsafe conditions and behaviours proactively before they escalate into incidents. During FY 2025-26, over 5 lakh safety observations were reported across the JSW Group, a scale that reflects deep organisational engagement with proactive hazard identification. Senior officer-level employees were institutionally embedded into structured safety observation and review cycles, ensuring that accountability for safety is not merely delegated but personally owned at the highest levels. This integration of leadership into routine safety processes reinforces the message from the boardroom to the shop floor that safety is a non-negotiable organisational priority. Findings from these observations are used to shape behavioural interventions, identify systemic gaps and drive continuous improvement. 

Transforming safety culture requires moving beyond procedural compliance towards a deeply internalised set of values. In FY 2025–26, we launched the ‘Lead the Change – Safety as a Core Value’ programme through which over 1,100 employees across all Steel and Coated Sites were trained to regard safety not as an externally imposed obligation but as a personal and organisational value. This initiative builds on the premise that durable safety performance is driven by intrinsic motivation where each individual becomes an active advocate for safety in their own work environment. 

### **Leadership Gemba Walks** 

Gemba Walks where senior leaders physically visit the point of work to observe, engage and act are a cornerstone of our visible leadership model. During FY 2025–26, structured Leadership Gemba Walks were conducted across all major sites, enabling senior management to directly observe ground conditions, engage in dialogue with workers, identify safety gaps in real time and model safety- 

conscious behaviours. These walks serve as a powerful mechanism for breaking down hierarchical barriers and creating a two-way conversation about safety. 

### **JSW Safety Quizathon** 

Building awareness of safety principles at scale requires engagement that is both broad and meaningful. During FY 2025–26, the JSW Group conducted a companywide Safety Quizathon that engaged over 13,000 employees across sites and functions. The Quizathon was designed not merely as a knowledge test but as an interactive platform to promote ownership of safety principles, share learnings and build a shared vocabulary around safe behaviours. By making safety awareness engaging and inclusive, the initiative strengthened the organisation’s collective safety consciousness. 

### **JSW Safety Assurance Protocol (JSAP)** 

In FY 2025–26, we launched the JSW Safety Assurance Protocol (JSAP), a comprehensive, structured assessment framework applied across all Steel and ISP sites. JSAP provides a systematic mechanism for evaluating safety governance maturity, compliance with Group Health and Safety Standards and the effectiveness of site-level safety management systems. By establishing a common baseline for safety assurance, JSAP enables the identification of improvement priorities and drives consistent, high-quality safety management across the organisation’s diverse operational footprint. 

### **Global engagement – worldsteel SHCO-17** 

Our leadership credentials in safety were further validated on the global stage in FY 2025-26, when our Company presented our holistic Contractor Safety Management framework at the worldsteel Safety, Health and Community Outreach (SHCO-17) conference in Istanbul. This presentation demonstrated our progress on the Vision 2030: Zero Harm journey to a global audience of steel industry peers, underscoring our ambition to be a global benchmark for health and safety performance in the metals and mining sector.

Process safety management at complex industrial facilities requires a structured methodology for understanding, monitoring and strengthening the barriers that prevent major accidents. We deployed the Bow-Tie Barrier Management methodology across Vijayanagar, Dolvi, BPSL and Salem, supported by expert-led training programmes. The Bow-Tie model enables the systematic identification of top process safety events, the mapping of preventive and mitigative controls (barriers), and the assessment of barrier effectiveness. 

In FY 2025–26, over 78,000 workmen underwent structured skill and competency assessments, a transformational increase from the 2,012 assessed in FY 2024–25, reflecting our Company’s decisive commitment to building a comprehensively assessed and verifiably competent workforce. These assessments cover critical safety domains including Lockout Tagout, Work at Height, Scaffolding, Machine Guarding, Conveyor Safety, Electrical Safety, Road Safety, Contractor Safety Management, Confined Space and Crane Safety evaluating both technical knowledge and practical application skills.

# **Digitalisation and innovation** 

Technology is a powerful force multiplier for safety management, enabling faster decision-making, broader reach, deeper analytics and more consistent compliance monitoring than is possible through manual processes alone. We have made digitalisation and innovation a defining pillar of our safety strategy, deploying a suite of cutting-edge tools and platforms that are transforming how safety is managed, monitored and learned across our operations. 

TapRooT<sup>®</sup> Advanced Root Cause Analysis (RCA) Team Leader Training, a globally recognised methodology for structured, comprehensive incident investigation. 

## **Abhigyan – industry-first conversational ai safety tool** 

In FY 2025–26, we achieved a landmark in industrial safety technology with the launch of ‘Abhigyan’ at Dolvi Steel, an industry-first conversational AI tool that provides employees and contract workers with real-time, multilingual access to our integrated safety standards. Abhigyan leverages advanced natural language processing to allow workers to query safety procedures, permit requirements, emergency protocols and regulatory standards in their preferred language, through a conversational interface that requires no technical expertise to use. 

TapRooT<sup>®</sup> provides investigators with a systematic framework for tracing incidents back to their root causes, whether in human factors, management systems, equipment or work environment and developing corrective actions that address these causes at their source. By building this capability internally, we ensure that every significant incident receives a thorough, unbiased investigation that drives genuine learning and lasting improvement. 

This innovation addresses one of the most persistent challenges in industrial safety, ensuring that all workers, including those with limited literacy or digital skills, have immediate access to the information they need to perform their work safely. Abhigyan democratises safety knowledge and eliminates language and literacy barriers as obstacles to safe behaviour.

Historically, paper-based PTW systems have been prone to errors, delays, inconsistency and loss of documentation, creating significant compliance risks.

key sites, digitising the entire permit lifecycle from application and approval to issuance, extension and closure. ### **UNSDGs** 



At JSW Steel, learning and capability development are being continuously reimagined to build a future-ready workforce equipped to thrive in an increasingly digital, dynamic and sustainability-driven environment. During FY 2025–26, we further strengthened our learning ecosystem through leadership development, digital learning platforms, strategic partnerships and targeted capability-building initiatives aligned with Industry 5.0 priorities. By fostering a culture of continuous learning, innovation and inclusive growth, we are empowering our people to enhance performance, accelerate transformation and drive long-term organisational excellence. 

## **Future-ready learning and capability building** 

## **Leadership excellence and Industry 5.0 readiness** 

FY 2025–26 marked a significant step forward in strengthening learning and capability development across our Company, with Learning & Development positioned as a strategic enabler of future readiness in alignment with Industry 5.0 priorities. Guided by insights from the My Learning Survey, our organisation adopted a blended learning approach designed to strengthen both technical and behavioural capabilities across all levels. 

The year witnessed several highimpact development initiatives aimed at strengthening leadership excellence, advancing inclusion and enhancing functional capability across our Company. The flagship AI Leadership Accelerator equipped senior leaders to leverage Generative and Agentic AI for strategic advantage while promoting responsible and ethical innovation. 

The Springboard programme, JSW Steel’s women leadership initiative, continued to strengthen the internal pipeline of women leaders through personalised development plans, mentoring support and action-learning projects. In parallel, the Sales Leadership Development Journey 2.0, delivered in partnership with Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad, further enhanced customer-centricity, business acumen and change leadership capabilities. Focused capability-building programmes across sales, commercial and technical functions also continued to deepen domain expertise aligned with evolving business priorities. 

The learning strategy focused on building adaptability, digital and data-driven decision-making, inclusive leadership, critical thinking and a growth mindset, supported by structured learning pathways and continuous feedback mechanisms. By embedding learning into day-to-day work and aligning capability development with organisational priorities, we are taking significant strides towards building an agile, resilient and future-ready workforce. 

We ensure that our workforce remains resilient and future-ready, capable of adjusting to technological advances, regulatory changes, and climate-driven transformations. This approach reduces the risk of disruption to both operations and livelihoods, while fostering a culture of continuous improvement and shared responsibility for sustainable growth. 

Our learning and development initiatives remained closely aligned with emerging business priorities such as digitalisation, automation and sustainability, reflecting our commitment to the human-centric principles of Industry 5.0. Programmes such as the AI Leadership Accelerator strengthened the strategic and responsible adoption of advanced technologies, enabling leaders to drive AIled transformation across the organisation. 

Data analytics and visualisation interventions further enhanced digital fluency at scale, supporting smarter, more efficient and sustainable decision-making. Leadership programmes also emphasised ethical technology adoption, inclusion and organisational agility, ensuring that automation complemented human capability rather than replacing it. Collectively, these initiatives strengthened a workforce capable of driving technological innovation while advancing long-term environmental, social and business sustainability objectives. 

## **Learning reimagined digitally** 

Digital platforms have reshaped learning at our Company by ensuring an agile, ondemand and personalised development ecosystem. Through platforms such as JSW Coursera, HBR Spark, Skillsoft, the JSW Steel Technical Academy and integrated digital learning pathways, employees can access global content, immersive labs and certifications in AI, analytics and domain expertise - anytime, anywhere. These digital learning journeys encourage self-paced development while enabling assessments, application-led assignments and datadriven insights to drive continuous improvement. The transition from episodic training to continuous capability building is accelerating rapid upskilling and reinforcing our Industry 5.0 vision of a human-centric, technologyenabled workforce. 



## **Strengthening capability through partnerships** 

External partnerships remain central to our capability-building strategy, providing access to world-class learning, global best practices and specialised expertise. Collaborations with Tier-1 institutes for leadership development journeys, alongside partnerships with leading global content providers such as Harvard, Skillsoft, Coursera and steelUniversity, ensure exposure to cutting-edge research, advanced skilling pathways and international benchmarking standards. These collaborations enable employees to pursue globally recognised certifications, engage with diverse industry perspectives and build capabilities that foster innovation, operational excellence and competitiveness in an increasingly dynamic business environment. 

## **Driving performance through continuous learning** 

Learning initiatives at JSW Steel have significantly strengthened performance and career progression across levels by embedding continuous capability building into the employee lifecycle. The Technical Academy, integrated into the GET induction programme has accelerated technical competency development and improved early-career performance, while digital learning aligned with the appraisal cycle has enabled targeted upskilling to support performance goals. Leadership development journeys culminate in Action Learning Projects that address real business challenges, often leading to enhanced responsibilities and accelerated career growth. Structured Individual Development Plan (IDP) discussions further support employees in identifying capability gaps and pursuing focused development pathways. 

The Technical Leaders Programme (TLP) and the JSW Steel Technical Academy together form the cornerstone of the Company’s future-ready capability ecosystem. The TLP develops high-potential technical talent into leaders who drive innovation, sustainability and operational excellence, while the Technical Academy offers personalised, role-based digital learning through globally benchmarked content.

# **JSW Centre on Climate Change and Health: Addressing climate change as a threat multiplier for public health** 

It is widely recognised in both academic and public health circles that climate change acts as a threat multiplier; and as such, it has the potential to aggravate a multitude of health risks, ranging from heat-related illnesses and respiratory conditions to vector-borne diseases and malnutrition. 

Consequently, effective climate change adaptation strategies must develop a nuanced understanding of how climate change exacerbates existing health challenges and institute proactive measures to mitigate these threats; as a failure to do so risks overwhelming public health systems, eroding their resilience, and disproportionately affecting vulnerable and marginalised groups such as the elderly, children, low-income communities, and those with pre-existing health conditions. In doing so, it spotlights our commitment to strengthening the adaptive capacity of the communities we serve against the multifaceted threats posed by climate change, particularly those related to health, and to fostering the development of evidence-based public health systems capable of maintaining resilience in the face of a warming planet.

# **Promoting holistic education by bridging the infrastructure gap** 

Tailoring educational curricula to meet the demands of an era marked by rapid digital transformation and providing a holistic learning experience require world-class infrastructure, including fully equipped science laboratories, cuttingedge computer labs, and well-maintained sports fields and courts. However, it is a sad reality that many schools across the nation lack access to even basic infrastructure such as adequate classrooms, reliable electricity, and clean sanitation facilities, let alone such advanced facilities. In the absence of these foundational resources, efforts to modernise education and nurture well-rounded students remain severely hamstrung. Therefore, we have set ourselves a mission to bridge this infrastructure gap by ensuring that schools across India are equipped with the essential tools and facilities necessary to foster academic excellence and holistic development. 

**Cultivating the Leaders of tomorrow: JSW ASPIRE, JSW Green Schools, and JSW Room to Read Initiatives** 

It is no overstatement to say that schooling is a life-defining experience. It not only equips individuals with the knowledge and skills required to build meaningful livelihoods in an increasingly competitive world but also enables us to develop the social and emotional intelligence necessary for forging strong social relationships and meaningfully contributing to society. Both primary and secondary education are therefore regarded as cornerstones of individual development and broader socio-economic upliftment. Regardless, millions of children across India continue to face persistent financial, geographic, infrastructural, and social barriers that stifle their access to quality education. 

To advance this goal, we run the School Infrastructure Project, which aims to revitalise aging schools with dilapidated facilities through upgrading existing infrastructure, new construction, and modern additions such as science laboratories, digital classrooms, and improved sanitation facilities. In doing so, this project creates inspiring and dignified learning environments where students can thrive. 

We remain committed to guaranteeing every child the right to a full education by eliminating the previously discussed obstacles. To further this goal, we have established multiple JSW-branded schools across India. These institutions, equipped with world-class infrastructure and staffed by experienced educators, are designed to offer students a holistic and future-ready education. To this end, they place a dual emphasis on developing enrolled students' foundational literacy and numeracy skills while simultaneously helping them cultivate the digital competencies needed to succeed in an increasingly technology-driven world. In doing so, these schools are not only providing children from often underserved communities with an equitable chance to unlock their full potential but also empowering them to become high-impact members of the Indian citizenry.

# **JSW Tamanna School: Empowering children with special needs** 

We firmly believe that every child, regardless of race, class, gender, or physical and mental abilities, deserves access to quality education that recognises and nurtures their unique potential. In line with this belief, we have established the JSW Tamanna School, a specialised institution dedicated to supporting children with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Situated at the OP Jindal Centre in Toranagallu, Karnataka, the school aims to foster the holistic development of enrolled students through personalised Individualised Education Plans (IEPs), which emphasise life skills, vocational training, and academic growth. The curriculum is designed not only to enhance cognitive abilities but also to foster social and emotional well-being, thereby enabling students to lead more independent and fulfilling lives. In addition to tailored teaching methods, the school offers a range of support services, including remedial education, speech and occupational therapy, and periodic health assessments conducted by specialists to monitor and address each child’s specific needs.

# **Water, Environment and Sanitation** 

Water, environment, and sanitation represent cross-cutting issues at the very heart of community well-being. Water security, a healthy environment, and robust sanitation are not only critical for sustaining human health and preventing communicable diseases but are also fundamental to economic growth, social equity, and environmental resilience. Therefore, we strive to implement targeted interventions that augment access to potable water, promote the responsible stewardship of sensitive ecosystems, and encourage the uptake of sound sanitation practices. Through such efforts, we aim to empower the communities we serve to lead healthier lives and foster the sustainable use and management of resources and ecosystem services to safeguard their availability for future generations. 

## **Improving climate resilience through water interventions** 



Climate change poses multifaceted physical risks, including but not limited to an increased frequency of extreme weather events and rising sea levels. Certain climate change-induced physical risks, such as the heightened occurrence and intensity of floods and droughts, can erode water security and thereby constrain communities' access to the freshwater resources essential for domestic use, agriculture, and sanitation, thereby undermining their socio-economic well-being. 

Recognising such threats, we have intensified our efforts aimed at equipping vulnerable communities with the tools, resources, and expertise needed to effectively adapt to shifting freshwater availability patterns effectuated by climate change. Over the past year, we implemented a range of initiatives focused on strengthening watershed management and storage infrastructure, establishing NbS, and constructing solar-powered bore wells. These solutions were strategically aligned with the goals of the Jal Jeevan Mission, a state-sponsored programme by the Government of India aiming to 

provide safe and adequate drinking water to every rural household, and they are playing a vital role in enhancing water security and building long-term resilience among populations disproportionately susceptible to climate change-associated water impacts.

## **Reconnecting communities with nature through tree plantation** 

It is well-established that human alienation from nature can exacerbate environmental degradation. In contrast, when individuals cultivate a deeper connection with the natural world, they often become more responsible stewards, learn to live in symbiosis with nature, and treat their environment with greater respect, care, and sensitivity. Acknowledging this relationship, we strive to help communities across the nation foster closer ties with nature and, in doing so, promote more eco-conscious behaviours. One of our key efforts involves organising large-scale tree plantation drives, where community members are invited to plant saplings carefully selected to align with local soil and climatic conditions. Through their participation in such initiatives, local communities not only develop closer ties with nature but also tangibly contribute to healthier and more resilient ecosystems. We have already conducted such drives near our ISP in Vijayanagar, at the Miyawaki forests in Vasind, and in the Mahavanam project in Salem. Over the coming years, we plan to expand these initiatives and organise similar drives in additional locations across the country.

# **Waste Management** 

India, by dint of its large population and extensive manufacturing activities, generates vast volumes of waste. If managed ineffectively, this waste can imperil human health and undermine ecosystem resilience. Several communities across the nation lack the infrastructure and know-how needed to safely dispose of waste. Therefore, our social sustainability strategy strives to furnish such underserved communities with the resources, knowledge, and infrastructure needed to manage waste in a responsible and environmentally conscious manner. 

## **Re-envisioning waste as value** 

We view waste-to-value schemes, which transform waste into economically valuable resources, as powerful, crosscutting solutions that simultaneously promote responsible waste management, create decent jobs, and accelerate socio-economic mobility. Therefore, this year, we intensified our efforts aimed at expanding these initiatives to underserved communities and providing them with the tools, training, and infrastructure required to convert waste into sustainable economic opportunities and adequate drinking water to every rural household, and they are playing a vital role in enhancing water security and building long-term resilience among populations disproportionately susceptible to climate change-associated water impacts. 







# **Skills and Livelihoods** 

The professional landscape is currently undergoing a tectonic shift driven by multiple factors, including the advent and rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence, evolving workforce expectations, an increasing emphasis on sustainability and digital transformation, and other political-economic influences. These macro trends are discernibly reshaping the quintessential repertoire of skills employees need to excel, with some skills gaining currency while others are being rendered obsolete. With this in mind, we remain committed to forging a future-ready Indian workforce by equipping existing and prospective employees, especially those from marginalised communities, with the skills necessary to thrive in this rapidly transforming professional landscape through a variety of upskilling initiatives. 

## **Empowering women and combating plastic pollution: Project Sakhi's Dual Impact** 

When considering the landscape of social, environmental, and economic problems in India, the issues of gender inequality and plastic pollution loom large. Project Sakhi represents a crosscutting initiative that seeks to simultaneously address these two pressing concerns. To this end, Project Sakhi employs women who learn traditional looming techniques to upcycle discarded items, such as plastic bags, gift wraps, and cassette tapes, and transform them into aesthetically pleasing and highly functional consumer products. In doing so, Project Sakhi not only enables beneficiaries to develop valuable looming skills and engage in well-paying work, but also helps tackle the multipronged environmental challenges posed by single-use plastic waste.

## **Bridging the gap between skills training and job outcomes with skill impact bonds** 

The Skill Impact Bond initiative, directly aligned with our mission of helping young Indians acquire the knowledge, skills, and experience needed to excel in an increasingly competitive professional landscape, is India’s pioneering development impact bond that places a two-pronged emphasis on both skills development and job placement. While most skill development initiatives across the nation primarily aim to equip young professionals with the capabilities required to be workforce-ready, the Skill Impact Bond goes one step further; it seeks to ensure that this training translates into measurable outcomes for participants by guaranteeing they secure meaningful employment opportunities that offer them the opportunity to bridge the gap between theory and practice by applying their newly acquired skills in real-world settings. 

This joint effort, executed in collaboration with several high-impact organisations including the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), the British Asian Trust (a coalition founded by HRH Prince Charles), the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation, the Children's Investment Fund Foundation, HSBC India, Dubai Cares, FCDO (UK Government), and USAID, aims to support 50,000 young professionals in India, 60% of whom are women. During FY 2025-26, the initiative benefitted 9,804 young professionals, reflecting continued progress in expanding opportunities and creating meaningful impact. 







# **Agri-livelihoods** 

Agriculture is the lifeblood of India. It forms the backbone of the Indian economy, sustains millions of livelihoods, strengthens food security, and drives rural development. That said, farmers across the nation are currently grappling with multifaceted socio-economic and environmental challenges, ranging from climate change and shifting rainfall patterns to soil degradation, water scarcity, and fluctuating market prices. 

In this context, we remain committed to helping farmers tackle these issues through sustainable solutions that not only improve their well-being but also enhance agricultural productivity, promote environmental resilience, and foster long-term rural prosperity. We have set an ambitious goal to benefit 1,00,000 farmers across India through targeted interventions focused on lowering input costs, boosting crop productivity, building stronger market linkages, and enhancing adaptive capacity to climate change-induced uncertainties. 

## **Strengthening last-mile access to quality agricultural inputs through FPOs** 

Recognising the challenges faced by small and marginal farmers in accessing quality agricultural inputs in a timely and cost-effective manner, the initiative leveraged Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) to create stronger village-level agricultural ecosystems. During FY 2025-26, the FPO network facilitated agri-input trade worth ₹4.63 crore through bulk procurement and local distribution of essential products, including quality seeds, fertilisers, plant protection chemicals, micronutrients and farm tools. Partnerships with leading agri-input companies further strengthened availability and ensured farmers received reliable and timely access to critical inputs. 

The initiative directly benefited 20,959 farmers by reducing dependence on intermediaries and lowering procurement costs through collective purchasing. Alongside improved access, farmers received guidance on selecting and scientifically applying inputs based on their crop requirements, enabling better decision-making and more efficient resource utilisation. The intervention contributed to lower cultivation costs, improved productivity and enhanced farm incomes, while reinforcing the role of FPOs as trusted institutions supporting resilient and sustainable rural livelihoods.

# **Art, culture and heritage** 

India is a nation steeped in a rich history of eclectic art forms, vibrant cultural traditions, and a heritage that spans thousands of years. Art, culture, and heritage are not only vital sources of national pride but also form a critical component of national identity and social cohesion. While they serve as a bridge connecting past and present, foster community resilience, and offer opportunities for employment and economic growth, they face the risk of erosion and gradual extinction in the absence of sustained preservation efforts and policies that recognise their intrinsic, cultural, and economic value. Hence, we have launched several initiatives that preserve traditional arts and crafts, revive those that have lost prominence, and empower artisans skilled in these time-honoured practices, thereby ensuring future generations have the opportunity to witness and bask in the pleasure of these cultural treasures for years to come. 

## **Where heritage inspires tomorrow** 

Set against the timeless backdrop of Hampi, home to the architectural grandeur and cultural legacy of the Vijayanagara Empire, JSW Foundation has created Hampi Art Labs, its flagship initiative dedicated to advancing art, culture and heritage. Located near JSW Steel’s Vijayanagar operations and launched in February 2024, the centre reflects over three decades of the Foundation’s commitment to preserving and promoting India’s cultural landscape. Founded by Sangita Jindal and Tarini Jindal Handa, Hampi Art Labs has been envisioned as an interdisciplinary institution where artists and creative practitioners can immerse themselves in a setting shaped by centuries of artistic excellence and cultural exchange. 

Spread across a nine-acre campus near the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Hampi, the centre brings together exhibition galleries, artist studios, landscaped gardens, residential facilities and collaborative spaces designed to nurture creativity. Through one- to three-month residency programmes, artists across disciplines are provided with world-class infrastructure, production capabilities and an inspiring environment to deepen their practice. Surrounded by the Tungabhadra River, dramatic boulder-strewn landscapes and the enduring spirit of one of India’s greatest civilisations, Hampi Art Labs stands as a living platform where heritage, nature and contemporary creativity converge to shape new cultural narratives. 



## **A new chapter for a timeless institution** 

As part of its commitment to preserving India’s cultural and architectural heritage, JSW Foundation has partnered with the David Sassoon Library and Reading Room through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to support the conservation and restoration of one of Mumbai’s most iconic institutions. Located in the historic Kala Ghoda precinct, the Grade I heritage structure, established in 1870, is among the city’s oldest surviving libraries and a landmark of enduring intellectual and cultural significance. Through technical and financial support, JSW Foundation is contributing to the revival of this historic institution, ensuring that its legacy continues to inspire future generations. 

The restoration initiative brings together a coalition of organisations, including Hermès, the Kala Ghoda Association, the Consulate General of Israel in Mumbai and other stakeholders to collectively safeguard this architectural treasure. Led by renowned conservation architect Abha Narain Lambah, the restoration aims to revive the library’s original character, preserving its distinctive buff-coloured trachyte and limestone architecture while enhancing its longevity. Through this initiative, JSW Foundation is helping transform heritage conservation into a shared endeavour, protecting not only a building, but a living repository of knowledge, memory and civic identity.

# **Sports promotion** 

We firmly believe that sports bind communities together, promote healthy lifestyles, and help individuals cultivate values such as teamwork, discipline, and perseverance. As the largest population in the world, India is inevitably home to immense untapped athletic talent across diverse regions and backgrounds. That said, several obstacles, including limited access to quality training facilities, inadequate coaching, socio-economic barriers, and lack of exposure to competitive platforms, remain in the way of harnessing this talent and realising their true athletic potential. Therefore, we have designed various sports programmes that seek to support India's top athletes' holistic development by identifying high-potential athletes and furnishing them with world-class infrastructure and coaching. These programmes cover the nation’s most widely followed and played sports, including swimming, badminton, basketball, football, boxing, and mallakhamb, and are delivered nationwide. 

## **Designed for Gold** 

Established in 2018, the Inspire Institute of Sport (IIS) reflects JSW Group’s belief that sport is nation-building infrastructure. Located in Vijayanagar and supported by a growing network of high-performance centres across India, IIS combines world-class facilities, sports science, elite coaching and holistic athlete development to create a structured pathway from grassroots talent to global competition. Backed by JSW Sports, the institute is advancing India’s Olympic ambitions through long-term investment, strategic partnerships and a high-performance ecosystem designed to transform potential into podium success across generations. 





## **Building stronger communities through sport** 

JSW Foundation continues to champion sport as a catalyst for youth empowerment, well-being and inclusive community development. Across Ballari District, Sandur Taluk and neighbouring regions, the Foundation has strengthened grassroots sporting ecosystems by creating opportunities for young people to build confidence, develop life skills and access structured sporting platforms. During FY 2025–26, its initiatives reached over 4,635 youth across rural and semi-urban communities through investments in sports infrastructure, community tournaments, school and college engagement programmes, and talent development pathways. Through sustained outreach, the Foundation promoted healthy lifestyles, sportsmanship and greater social inclusion where access to organised sport remains limited. 

The Foundation supported a wide range of sporting activities spanning cricket, volleyball, kabaddi, kho-kho, table tennis, shuttle badminton and collegiate competitions. Community tournaments across villages such as Talur, Taranagar, Toranagallu, Vaddu and Bannihatti engaged thousands of participants and strengthened local sporting culture through provision of equipment, uniforms and recognition platforms. Beyond grassroots engagement, support extended to district-, state- and national-level sporting events, contributing to achievements such as the Karnataka Senior Rokit Ball teams reaching the national semi-finals and the JSW Volleyball Team securing Gold at an All-India Championship. Early-age participation was also encouraged through school programmes and distribution of sports kits to students, fostering discipline, teamwork and long-term sporting aspirations.

We view the protection of human rights not merely as a compliance requirement but as a core expression of our values and commitment to promoting diversity, equity and inclusion and uplifting the communities in which we operate. 

In line with our commitment to operationalising the triple bottom line framework, which treats people, planet, and profit as equally vital measures of business success, we strive to treat every individual connected to our operations, be it employees, business partners, contract workers, or surrounding communities with dignity, respect, and fairness. 

## **Objective** 

Balance the needs, interests, and expectations of all stakeholders with business priorities, while safeguarding the welfare of communities where we operate and consistently upholding human rights across the value chain. 

To translate this belief into meaningful action, we have built a robust human rights governance structure anchored in four key pillars: building awareness across the value chain, identifying and evaluating potential risks, designing targeted mitigation strategies, and ensuring continuous oversight through regular progress reviews. This structured approach enables us to move beyond intent and embed human rights considerations into the fabric of our day-to-day decision-making across all operational levels. 

## **Progress towards** 

**the objective** Achieved 100% Human Rights Due Diligence (HRDD) coverage across all ISPs and mines.

# **Approach to human rights management** 

Our approach to human rights management is grounded in the conviction that respecting and protecting human rights is an active, ongoing responsibility—not merely a passive obligation satisfied by regulatory compliance alone. To instil this conviction at the heart of our operational ethos, we have adopted a comprehensive Policy on Protecting Human <u>Rights, supported by an internal Technical Standard that provides operational guidance</u> on identifying material human rights issues, assigning accountability, and implementing effective management systems and procedures across our operations. 

Our human rights framework ensures full compliance with all applicable national and international laws, regulations, and standards, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the core conventions of the International Labor Organization, and the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples. We also transparently disclose our human rights performance through the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) standards, against the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs), and under Principle 5 of the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct (NGRBC) as part of our Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR). 

Our commitment to human rights is further reinforced by three interrelated policies that govern how we engage with our workforce, our communities, and our broader value chain: the Policy on Labour Practices and Employment Rights, the Policy on Enhancing Equality, <u>Diversity and Inclusivity, and the Policy on Business Conduct. In tandem with our Policy</u> on Protecting Human Rights, these policies form a cohesive governance architecture that embeds respect for human rights into the way we operate, make decisions, and conduct business at every level of our organisation.
